pages.name: The gap across a pole
pages.text: A second set runs beside a live board. Its breaker is open. Before it closes, it must match the board in four things: voltage, frequency, phase sequence and phase angle. Each pole has a board phase on one side and the set's same phase on the other. On a 440 V board each phase is 254 V. What the pole sees is the difference between them. That is the voltage across the pole. The set's wave runs 40° ahead. So the pole sees 2 sin 20° × 254 = 174 V.

pages.task: The set's wave runs 60° ahead of the board's. Each phase is 254 V. What voltage appears across each pole?
pages.why: 2 × sin 30° × 254 = 2 × 0.5 × 254 = 254 V. That is a whole phase voltage.

pages.name: Slip
pages.text: Now the set runs 0.2 Hz faster than the board. That frequency difference is the slip. The set's waves gain one whole cycle every 1 ÷ 0.2 = 5 s. So the angle creeps round, and the gap swells and shrinks every 5 s. The three lamps glow and go dark together. The dial is a synchroscope. Its pointer turns once each slip cycle. It turns clockwise when the set runs fast. It stands at 12 when the angle is zero.

pages.name: One turn
pages.task: The set runs at 60.25 Hz on a 60 Hz board. How long does the pointer take to go once round?
pages.why: The slip is 60.25 − 60 = 0.25 Hz. The set gains a quarter of a cycle each second. So a whole cycle takes 1 ÷ 0.25 = 4 s.

pages.name: A close out of step
pages.text: Suppose the breaker shuts a quarter turn out. Shut at 90°, each pole sees 359 V. The reactances of the set and the board are the main limit on the surge that gap drives. Here it is 5.7 per unit. The surge also yanks the rotor into step. That puts 4.0 per unit of torque through the shaft and coupling. Shut at 180° and the surge reaches 8.0 per unit. That is more than a three-phase fault at the set.

pages.name: Bottom of the dial
pages.task: Both voltmeters read 440 V. The pointer is at the bottom of the dial, at 180°. It is turning slowly. Can you close?
pages.answer: No, each pole sees about twice the phase voltage
pages.why: At 180° the waves are opposite. Each pole sees 2 × sin 90° × 254 = 508 V. That gives the biggest surge of all. Wait for the pointer to come round to 12.

pages.name: The advance angle
pages.text: A breaker takes a set time to shut after the command. Say 50 ms. At 0.2 Hz slip the pointer turns 360 × 0.2 = 72° a second. In 50 ms it moves 72 × 0.05 = 3.6°. So if you press Close at 12, the breaker shuts 3.6° past it. Instead, send the close 3.6° before 12. That lead is the advance angle. The dial shows both. The first close lands 3.6° past 12. The second, sent 3.6° early, lands at 12.

pages.name: Late by
pages.task: The set runs 0.5 Hz fast. The breaker takes 50 ms. You press Close just as the pointer passes 12. How many degrees past 12 does the breaker shut?
pages.why: 360 × 0.5 = 180° a second. 180 × 0.05 = 9°. Pressing at 12 lands 9° late. So the close should go 9° early.

pages.name: Phase sequence
pages.text: Two of the set's phases, B and C, are now swapped. The lamps no longer dim together. One goes dark while the other two blaze. The dark lamp runs round the three in turn. When lamp A is dark, lamps B and C each see 440 V. The pointer turns exactly as before. It compares only phase A on each side. So it cannot see the order of the other two. The wiring fixes the phase sequence. It is the phase rotation you already test.

pages.name: Crossed phases
pages.task: The pointer turns slowly through 12. Lamp A is dark, but lamps B and C are bright. Can you close?
pages.answer: No, the phase sequence is wrong
pages.why: With the sequence right, all three lamps go dark together. Here B and C blaze at 440 V while A is dark. So B and C are crossed. Put the wiring right first.

pages.name: The relay
pages.text: With a relay in charge, Close only asks. The relay closes only inside its window. Here it is 10°, 0.2 Hz and 2% of voltage. Makers set it anywhere from 0.5% to 5% on voltage and 0.1 to 0.5 Hz on slip. At 0.5 Hz slip it refuses and says why. At 60.10 Hz it agrees. It waits for the advance angle, 1.8°, and sends the close. The breaker shuts at 12. An automatic synchroniser also trims the governor and the AVR, by moving their set points.

pages.name: Trim before closing
pages.task: The set reads 420 V and 60.40 Hz. The board is 440 V, 60 Hz. What do you trim before closing?
pages.answer: Raise the field, and lower the fuel a little
pages.why: More field raises the voltage towards 440 V. Less fuel slows the set until the pointer turns slowly enough to catch at 12.

pages.name: Advance for 80 ms
pages.task: A relay must shut a breaker at 12. The set runs 0.3 Hz fast. The breaker takes 80 ms. How many degrees before 12 does the relay send the close? Give it to one decimal place.
pages.why: 360 × 0.3 = 108° a second. 108 × 0.08 = 8.64°. To one decimal place that is 8.6°.
